QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_44

question.text: Under SAS-500, 'climate-resilience' outcomes are hard to measure within a 3-year ZCZP horizon because:

answer.text: Climate impacts unfold over decades, making short-horizon attribution statistically weak; the SIA should report PROXY resilience indicators (adaptive-capacity index, early-warning coverage, diversified-livelihood adoption) rather than claim final climate-impact reduction

explanation.text: The Logic: Climate outcomes materialise over decades; a 3-year ZCZP cannot measure actual climate impact. The SIA should report proxy resilience indicators (adaptive capacity, EWS coverage, livelihood diversification) and be explicit about the horizon mismatch in the Limitations section. The Trap: Options A, C, D are factually wrong. Cross-Exam Context: Horizon-mismatch logic also in XIX (AIF — fund-life vs investment-horizon) and X-A / X-B (Investment Adviser — goal-horizon planning). Assessor's Pro-Tip: For climate-resilience programmes, anchor the Report in proxy/adaptive-capacity indicators, not 'degree-of-warming-avoided'. The latter is unauditable in a 3-year window.
